Report Details

Violation Code: 78.61(c)1 - DISPOSAL OF DRILL CUTTINGS - Owner or operator disposed of drill cuttings from below the casing seat, in a pit that does not meet the requirements of 25 Pa. Code Sections 78.62(a)(5)-(18) and Section 78.62(b).
Violation ID: 950892
Permit API: 129-26012
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Rostraver Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 4/07/2022
Comments: This admin inspection is being conducted in response to review of 3rd party consultant, Moody and Associates, Inc., investigation report for the Manack 2 Well Site in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County. Review of DEP inspections, Moody's investigation report and ES plans for the well site were conducted. In IR 3011479 and IR 3310984, drill cutting pit locations and waste manifests were requested and were unable to be obtained, due to the well site transfer from Atlas Resources to Diversified Oil and Gas. Diversified OG suspected the drill cuttings were land farmed which corroborated with the well site's ES plan. However, in Moody's report, they identified the approximate locations of the cuttings pit by increasing the the vertical exaggeration of the terrain in Good Earth and confirming with land owner upon a site visit conducted March 19th, 2020. The drill pit was located approximately 50 ft northwest of the well. Results reported by DEP and Moody's indicated elevated metal concentrations and pH levels in several locations around the well site. Due to reported lab results and identification of drill pit by Moody, the Department recommends that the Operator evaluate the integrity of the drill pit. Based on DEP sample results and Moody's investigation report, violations are being issued under 78.61 and 78.62.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/27/2023 to ARMAC RESOURCES LLC in Warren City, Warren county. 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/27/2023
Violation Code: 78.91(a) - PLUGGING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Upon abandoning a well, the owner or operator failed to plug the well to stop the vertical flow of fluids or gas within the well bore under 25 Pa. Code §§ 78.92—78.98 or an approved alternate method.
Violation ID: 1000074
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 6/27/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration case (CTS# 369563). Previously this well was found to have methane detected outside of the well bore and the operator decided to plug the well. Upon completion of their plugging attempt they inadvertently cemented some of their tubing into the well. Subsequently a camera was ran into the well and bubbles were visibly seen at the top of fluid level. A MSA Altair 5X gas meter was used and determined the bubbles were methane being emitted into the well bore. A violation was issued to the operator for not properly plugging the well. To address this violation the operator is having a rig drill down to approx 550', which is 50' below the surface casing shoe and remove the cemented in tubing at which point another camera run will take place to see if the well is still bubbling methane. Today's operations: Bull Run Rig 118 drilled from 360.88 to 394.28 with a 4" coring bit.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 9/02/2026 to SCORPIO ENERGY INC in Howe Township, Forest county. 102.4(b)5 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – The E & S Plan did not contain the required drawings and narrative.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SCORPIO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 9/02/2026
Violation Code: 102.4(b)5 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS – The E & S Plan did not contain the required drawings and narrative.
Violation ID: 8287773
Permit API: 053-31161
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: This site is undergoing construction for the development of a conventional well. The drilling permit and E and S Plan are posted at the entrance of the location. There was no activity on the location at the time of this inspection. The template for the site and access road has been completed. The gathering lines for this well have been buried within the template of the road. Stone has not yet been applied to any portion of the road or well site. The E and S Plan that was prepared for this site is inadequate as it does not account for all surface waters of the Commonwealth that converge with the earth disturbance associated with the construction of this well site and the access road that leads to it. In addition, the site and access road have been excavated significantly below the natural grade, therefore, watercourses that were likely below the surface prior to construction are now present at the surface and are not accounted for in the E and S Plan. Due to the insufficient plan and construction practices, the BMPs that have been installed are insufficient and are promoting stormwater to become concentrated and directed into waters of the Commonwealth. Numerous waters of the Commonwealth are also being removed from their natural channel and redirected.The ditches along the access road do not consist of a durable material, nor have they been stabilized to account for the flow of water running through them and have become significantly eroded due to the volume and velocity of stormwater and surface water. Aside from the lack of stabilization measures in the ditch, the roadside banks and perimeter of the location (that do not appear to require any additional excavation) have also not yet been stabilized. No perimeter BMPs (such as silt sock) have been installed for minimizing the amount of sediment leaving the un-stabilized areas of earth disturbance. The culverts that have been installed at the intermittent streams have been poorly installed. There is excessive excavation at the inlets and outlets of these water features resulting in sediment entering the stream channels. The E and S Plan does not account for headwall protection at these culverts, therefore, the disturbed earth near the inlets and outlets is vulnerable to scouring and erosion into the water channel. Improper installation and the lack of energy dissipators at the outlets of the installed cross-pipes that are conveying stormwater is resulting in scouring at the outlets of these culverts and increasing the amount of accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Since no stone has been placed on the road, recent traffic on the road template after rain events has caused the template to become soft and appreciably rutted in spots. This has allowed stormwater, and in some areas, the flow from a watercourse to flow onto the road template. As a result of these deficiencies, there has been accelerated erosion across the earth disturbance associated with the construction of the access road and well site. Significant amounts of sediment have discharged into and remain accumulated in spring seeps and unnamed tributary of Hastings Run.In addition to the E and S deficiencies, due to the abundance of shallow ground water at the site, the use of pits for temporary containment or permanent encapsulation of cuttings or any residual waste from this well in a pit would not satisfy the requirements outlined in Chapter 78.56(a)(8), unless Scorpio Energy can demonstrate otherwise to the Department in advance of lining the pit.The deficiencies noted above also apply to the first well location (Well Site 56) and the access road getting to that site. Corrective action should be applied to both sites in order to remediate the noted violations and to return to compliance.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. Permit API: 015-23674
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Franklin Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2/11/2022
Comments: This Inspection Report cites violations for an apparent flowback (brine) release to the pad surface. The Analytical Report (attached) for SAC 942 metals shows 16.7 mg/L barium and 80.6 mg/L strontium in the liquid sample collected on February 1, 2022 (inspection 3315684). The narrative and findings in this report are from that previous inspection. I spoke with Justin Myers (Chief) on site. He explained that Cudd started drilling out plugs from the 5 Marcellus well heads today. They will have 3 coil tubing units on site to complete this job. Myers expects they will finish drilling the plugs in about 10 days. Workers are removing liner containment used while hydraulically fracturing the 5 Marcellus wells at this site. Pooled liquid on the south half of the pad surface has electrical conductivity of 14.1 - >19.99 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. I collected liquid sample 0935-430 in a 125 mL bottle and sent it to the DEP lab for SAC 942 metals analysis. The puddles across the south end of the pad are relatively shallow (<1/2" deep), so I did not fill a 500 mL bottle for inorganic element analysis. Violations could be cited pending laboratory sample analysis. Myers contacted Brendon Logan (Chief) to investigate the pooled liquid on the pad surface. I did not observe accelerated erosion or sedimentation during this inspection. Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Air temp 26F JLP

Report Details

Violation ID: 8268223
Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/19/2026
Comments: On March 19, 2026, the DEP conducted a Follow Up Inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, 4157162, 4157480, and 4157532. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports and discusses 8 observed culverts along the access road as well as any observed erosion and sedimentation issues along the access road. This Inspection Report is Inspection 1 of 2 and assesses Culverts 1-5. All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/18/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8249812
Permit API: 117-20505
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Charleston Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/18/2025
Comments: On 9/18/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a follow-up incident inspection in response to complaint #389073 at the Seneca Vandergrift 290 well site located in Charleston Twp, Tioga Co. It was 46 degrees and mostly cloudy when I arrived on site. Rainfall has not impacted the region in the last 48 hours.There are four active wells on site staged for production along with two that are in the process of being plugged. The Vandergrift 290 2H and 5H wells have had recent plugging operation and a plugged well monument has been installed on the 2H well, plugged date 12/4/2024. The area that was excavated around and north of the well cellars remains open along with the areas on the fill slope and across the grassy field north of the pad. Elevated conductance above 4000 uS was found in soils in the bottoms of the 2H, 3H, 5H, and 6H well cellars. The highest reading found in the 4H well cellar was 1385 uS conductance in the soil and 1035 uS conductance in the water. The highest reading witnessed in the 1H well cellar was 1230 uS conductance. Elevated conductance readings were also found at the north edge of the pad, above the east and west excavated areas of the fill slope. I did witness a wet area of soil 10 feet up from the base of the fill slope and within the approximate center of the west excavated area that field tested above 4000 uS conductance. Liquid flowing down through the excavated area below the fill slope and into the catch basin sump field tested at 1229 microsiemens conductance. Liquid in the sump field tested at 1481 microsiemens conductance and liquid flowing out of the sump field tested at 1693 microsiemens conductance.Temporary compost filter socks that were installed at the base of the fill slope and in the excavated area of the field on the north side of the location that do have sediments above 50% of the height of the sock. Temporary stabilization that has been applied to the fill slope and the excavated area of the field needs to be refreshed. Erosional channels were evident on the fill slope and within the excavated area of the the field.Violations are still outstanding for inspection IDs 399274 and 4029808 for a release of an unknown amount of produced water to the unprotected pad surface, to the unprotected grassy field below the fill slope and flowing offsite during plugging operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Continue monitoring the area for contamination.2. Continue remediation efforts as necessary. 3. Continue collecting fluids that demonstrate elevated conductance on the well pad, in the excavated areas around the well cellars, in seeps from the fill slope, in the collection sump at the northwest corner of the location and other areas on the location as discovered.4. Assess the temporary compost filter socks and temporary stabilization. Apply maintenance as necessary.I left the site at 1130 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-01 to Msl Oil & Gas Corp in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. SWMA 302(B)1 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to use methods or facilities necessary to control leachate, runoff, discharges and emissions from residual waste in accordance with DEP regulations.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Msl Oil & Gas Corp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-01
Violation Code: SWMA 302(B)1 - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person failed to use methods or facilities necessary to control leachate, runoff, discharges and emissions from residual waste in accordance with DEP regulations.
Violation ID: 883846
Permit API: 083-47035
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-01
Comments: Brian Ayers of DEP was contacted by MSL's Dick Pascarella on 4/23/2020 regarding a condensate leak from a tank that was found that day. PA Fish and Boat Commission officer Tom Mcmann was on site 4/24/2020 to follow up and took some photos that are included in this report. It appears as though a small, uncontained drip gas tank had a failure at a fitting at some point prior to the spill being found. This tank holds mostly water that condenses from the gas coming from the compressor station nearby, but also contains some condensed petroleum liquids. An estimated 5-10 gallons of this fluid escaped from the broken fitting and was spilled to the ground. Some of this ran down slope toward an UNT of Chappel Fork, with some collecting in a low, wet area and a small amount eventually entering the water. Tom Mcmann documented photos of the condensate in the vernal pool area, which is included in the attached photos. A Department site visit was performed 5/1/2020. The operator has scraped up the surface of the contaminated site, and placed down straw mulch and seed. They also put down gravel around equipment close to the stream and have built containment around the drip gas tank. The area close to the stream was observed to have a strong condensate odor and some sheen could be spotted entering the stream when this area was agitated on the stream banks. Some product was noted, mostly in the form of sheen, in the UNT Chappel Fork. The stream crosses Chappel Fork Rd a few feet from where the product entered, and sheen was visible upon agitation approximately 150-200 feet downstream. No free product was apparent and no other waters were impacted. The operator was contacted and instructed to place booms for containment and monitor through the weekend, followed by a run of agitating the stream bottom to push any product caught in the substrate to collect it in the next week. They also dug up the impacted soil next to the stream with shovels and removed it. Bill Otto of MSL sent photos to show that booms were placed and digging done as of late Friday, May 1. Further followup will be done as possible.

Comments: On November 7, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Burkett well site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. This inspection was conducted in response to Stimulation notifications that were submitted by the operator on October 31, 2025. Stimulation operations were scheduled to begin on November 4, 2025, for wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated for this site on August 12, 2020.The following was observed during this inspection:Upon starting this inspection, the Department spoke with Halliburton representative Phillip Gonzalez, who cautioned the Department about the hazards present on site, such as moving vehicles and high-pressure lines. Wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H appear to be undergoing stimulation operations simultaneously at the time of inspection (photos 8 and 9). Five additional well heads are onsite that appear to be in production (photo 7).The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 15). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 16). All other containers and machinery onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 2 and 10). The well pad containment appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no tears observed. Range Resources representative Justin Fedor was onsite during this inspection who provided the secondary containment inspection log upon request (photo 11). No evidence of fluid leaks was observed from the portion of the MCC Partners to Burkett Temporary Waterline (TWL) at the well pad (photo 12). The Act 9 sign is located at the access road entrance and is not obscured from vegetation, in accordance with 78a55 requirements (photo 24). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness and Contingency (PPC) plan, well permits, and safety data sheets are located onsite (photos 17-20). However, the PPC plan is not specific to this site. The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. The access road and well pad were muddy during this inspection with little observable gravel (photos 1 and 23). This appears to be causing sedimentation from the access road to occur in the rock-lined channel along the access road (photos 21 and 22). This sedimentation appears to continue downslope for approximately 20 feet along the access road and stops within the boundaries of the well site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the accumulating sediment from the access road in the rock-lined channel.Violations are to be issued in IR 4091983 for failure to have a site-specific PPC plan on site and for failure to maintain the access road which resulted in sedimentation.

The elevated pooled water was observed behind the produced fluid tank.The DEP spoke with Expand representative Mike Deming via phone and he stated their consultants visited the site the same day and confirmed the elevated water around the produced fluid tank. The release was then reported to the DEP via the 24 hour number. Expand will begin remediation on 10/09/2025. The quantity of the release is unknown. The following reoccurring violations are cited against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Due to the unknown quantity of the release this will be referred to Act 2 for compliance. The following violations remain open against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.I departed at 1125 hours.

Violations of Clean Streams Law 401 are cited at this time for discharging sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth. I departed the site at 1430.

Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

Comments: On July 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 gas well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County following IR 4209208, where violations were continued for broken and corroded piping causing a release, as well as the issuance of new violations for inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site.Accompanying on today's inspection is DEP ET Rosie Wise.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appear to be unchanged from IR 4209208, and to date, a Notice of Violation Operator response has yet to be received.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the gas wellhead with all required information posted on it, however the well tag does not appear to updated and the phone number listed on the tag is not in service. Violations are being continued at this time for having inaccurate information on the well tag/posting. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the gas wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a small production tank adjacent to the gas wellhead, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this tank. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site. The tank on the left was observed to be green and the tank on the right was observed to be a faded green color. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the green (left) production tank on site, however, the faded green (right) production tank was observed to have several corroded pipes connected to it. Towards the top of the faded green (right) production tank, the Department observed an area where severe corrosion caused piping to break off. This broken pipe was observed to be on the ground at the base of the production tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this broken pipe, from the other corroded pipes still connected to the production tank, or the production tank at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the area at the base of the faded green production tank ((3.80 mS and Over Range (>12mS)) and adjacent to the broken corroded pipe (0.329 mS). These conductivity readings were compared to a background soil conductivity reading of 0.181 mS collected upslope and away from the release area. The soil conductivity readings in the release area are elevated compared to background subjugating that the release from the back of the production tank on the right has yet to be remediated. Violations are being continued at this time for the release from the production tank.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to remove production equipment not in use from the gas well site. The Department is again requesting the Operator provide the Department with a Notice of Violation Operator response within 14 days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for a release from corroded and broken piping, inaccurate information on the well tag, and failure to remove production equipment not currently in use from the gas well site is to remain outstanding at this time.

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-23
Comments: Weather was 74 degrees and sunny. Met with Chief representative Jon Hafer on location. Well was in production. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached to the production casing reading 2136 PSI. Well had a 0 to 5k PSI analog pressure gauge attached to the production manifold reading approximately 2050 PSI. Well had 2 annulus vents plumbed to a shared poly-tank with the East 1H. Samples were taken from the annulus vents by both Chief and the DEP. 100% LEL and 100% methane was detected on the 5 1/2" X 9 5/8" annulus vent. 100% LEL and 7% methane was detected on the 9 5/8" X 13 3/8" annulus vent. 0% combustable gas was detected anywhere around the well at time of inspection. A sample of production gas was taken off the payline by both Chief and the DEP.
